whyWrong.vas: 'tu vas manger' means 'you're going to eat', not 'you must'.

whyWrong.faut: faut is impersonal — it only ever takes il ('il faut'); with nous it's devons.
whyWrong.devez: That's the vous form — nous devons.

whyWrong.va: 'elle va cuisiner' means 'she's going to cook', not 'she can'.
whyWrong.faut: faut is impersonal ('il faut'); it can't take 'elle' as its subject.

items.fullSentence: Pour rester en bonne santé, il faut manger équilibré.
items.sentenceTrans: To stay healthy, you need to eat a balanced diet.

whyWrong.tu peux: 'You can' — the sentence states a necessity: il faut.
whyWrong.tu devrais: 'You should' (conditional) — a general necessity is il faut.
whyWrong.il devrait: 'It should' — the set phrase for necessity is il faut.

items.fullSentence: Pour être en forme, il faut faire du sport.
items.sentenceTrans: To be in shape, one must do sport.

whyWrong.dois: dois goes with tu — here it's the impersonal il faut.
whyWrong.peut: pouvoir says it's possible, not necessary — il faut.
whyWrong.va: That would be a plan (going to), not a necessity — il faut.

items.fullSentence: Vous devez étudier pour le quiz.
items.sentenceTrans: You must study for the quiz.

whyWrong.devons: That's the nous form — vous devez.
whyWrong.doivent: That's the ils form — vous devez.
whyWrong.dois: That's the je/tu form — vous devez.

items.sentenceAfter: prendre le bus pour aller au marché.
items.fullSentence: Tu peux prendre le bus pour aller au marché.
items.sentenceTrans: You can take the bus to go to the market.

whyWrong.peut: That's the il/elle form — tu peux.
whyWrong.pouvez: That's the vous form — tu peux.
whyWrong.veux: vouloir is wanting — the suggestion is tu peux (you can).

whyWrong.doit: That's the singular elle form — elles doivent.
whyWrong.devez: That's the vous form — elles doivent.
whyWrong.devons: That's the nous form — elles doivent.
